f1.quote: Induce a two-phase microstructure by adding a fourth element (such as Al or Ti) and applying a heat treatment to promote precipitation or ordering, resulting in the formation of a secondary magnetic phase (e.g., bcc or ordered intermetallic) within the fcc matrix.

f5.quote: Presence of a second magnetic phase (bcc or ordered intermetallic) dispersed within the fcc matrix, leading to phase boundaries and precipitates.

f8.quote: The second phase acts as a domain wall pinning site and introduces additional magnetic anisotropy, thereby increasing the coercive field by hindering domain wall motion.

f11.quote: Coercive field will increase significantly, exceeding 100 Oe (potentially reaching several hundred Oe), compared to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its matched derivatives.
